description: Installs alongside stock Google Maps under its own package name. On by default, because stock Maps comes built into most phones and cannot be replaced by a patched copy.
name: Change package name

options.description: The package name to install under. Must be a valid Android package name. Left at org.ungoogled.android.apps.maps, Add microG support installs under org.ungoogled.android.apps.maps.microg instead.
options.title: Package name

description: Adds a Customization row under Settings on the account sheet, with switches for the patches here that can be turned back off inside the app.
name: Customization screen

description: Adds an Experimental row to your profile's menu, under Edit profile and Share profile, that opens an Experimental screen.
name: Experimental screen

description: Waze's dark mode in true black for AMOLED screens: the app's dark backgrounds are black, and with Black night map the night map's background too. Roads, labels, buttons and text keep their colours.
name: Full black

options.description: The night map's background black as well. Skipped by Morphe Manager 1.35 and other patcher 1.15+ builds, which would crash Waze when the map opens; patch with Morphe Desktop to get it.
options.title: Black night map

description: Removes the sponsored pins on the map and on Android Auto, the full-screen ads shown while you are stopped, and the ad statistics Waze sends.
name: Hide ads

description: Hides promoted map pins and "Sponsored" search results, Gemini's AI summaries ("Know before you go" and the review summary), the row of businesses under an address on its place sheet, the home tab's Explore feed and the Explore / Contribute / You tabs. Each can be switched back on on the Customization screen.
name: Hide ads and clutter

description: Uses the flat multicolour pin Maps had before the 2025 gradient icon as the launcher icon and on the screen Maps opens with. With Add microG support, microG's C sits in the pin's circle.
name: Legacy icon

description: Adds a Location source choice to the Customization screen: Android's own location providers, microG's (microg Services) or Google Play services' fused provider. With Android, neither is ever asked for a location. A source that is missing or disabled is never used, so location keeps working without it. Also keeps the network (Wi-Fi/cell) provider registered when no fused provider answers, instead of GPS only, so a fix does not go stale indoors.
name: Location provider toggle

options.description: The location source Maps starts with. On: the fused provider -- Google Play services', or microG's in microG Maps -- whenever it is installed and enabled, Android's own providers otherwise. Off: Android's own providers. Can be changed later on the Customization screen.
options.title: Default to Play services location

description: The old Waze mods' map skin, as changes to Waze's own: bigger map labels, a wider navigation arrow head and a warm day background. The night background is Full black's. Skipped by Morphe Manager 1.35 and other patcher 1.15+ builds, which would crash Waze when the map opens; patch with Morphe Desktop to get it.
name: Map skin

options.description: Waze: 14.
options.title: Map labels: huge

options.description: Waze: 12.
options.title: Map labels: big

options.description: Waze: 10.
options.title: Map labels: medium

options.description: Waze: 8.
options.title: Map labels: small

options.description: As a multiple of the arrow's tail width. Waze: 3.0.
options.title: Navigation arrow head width

options.description: Waze: fafcfa, near white.
options.title: Day map background (hex)

description: How far ahead Android Auto gives its heads-up, and how long a jam must last before the traffic bar shows it. The defaults are the old Waze mods' (Chuppito).
name: Navigation distances

options.description: Waze: 200 m.
options.title: Android Auto heads-up, normal roads (m)

options.description: Waze: 500 m.
options.title: Android Auto heads-up, freeways (m)

options.description: Waze: 360 s.
options.title: Traffic bar: time in traffic (s)

description: Turns off conversational reporting, Waze's Gemini voice assistant for reports, together with its activation dialog, tips and onboarding.
name: No AI reporting

description: Keeps Google Assistant out of Waze: no Assistant button, onboarding or settings entry, whatever Waze's server enables for your region.
name: No Google Assistant

description: Save places without a Google account, kept only on the phone: Save opens Maps' own "Place saved" sheet (Want to go, Travel plans, Starred places, Favorites, your own lists, a note), and a "Local saved" row on the account sheet rebuilds Maps' You tab -- your recent places, your lists and labels (Home, Work, your own) -- with export and import (backup file, KML, Google Takeout's saved lists and Saved Places.json, several files or the whole Takeout .zip at once). It also has a Timeline: where the phone has been, grouped into days and visits, kept only on the phone, with GPX export. Recording is off until switched on there; it shows a notification while it runs. With Add microG support, Maps' own Save keeps syncing to your account and Local saved instead copies the account's saved lists to the phone (Pull from Google account).
name: Offline saved places

description: Brings the Pixel-only power saving mode to every phone: while driving with navigation, press the power button and Maps shows only key information such as the next turn on a black screen. Turn it on or off in Settings > Navigation > Power saving mode. Pixels that have it built in keep Google's own version unless Power saving mode is turned on in Power Saving Options, a row on the account sheet under Customization, which also has: a navigation button that opens the power saving screen without locking the phone, switching to it by itself when idle, a speedometer on it, a lower frame rate, and its black map in navigation or all over Maps.
name: Power saving mode

description: Adds a Proxy screen to Customization that sends Maps' own traffic, map data included, through an HTTP proxy -- for example Orbot's (127.0.0.1:8118) to use Tor. Map data never falls back to a direct connection: if the proxy stops, Maps stops loading. Needs a recent Play services network engine (Cronet); Maps warns when it cannot take the proxy.
name: Proxy

description: Squares off rounded corners across the UI, including the two round navigation buttons.
name: Rectangle shapes

description: Adds a Remember filter states switch to the Experimental screen. With it on, the trail filters you set (length, elevation, rating, difficulty, activities, features and the rest, but not Distance away) stay set when you go back to the home screen and after the app restarts, instead of resetting.
name: Remember filters

description: Removes permissions that only serve Google-account features or Google's data collection: background location, physical activity, contacts, microphone (voice search stops working), camera (Lens and Live View stop working), car speed, advertising ID, push messages and Google services settings. Left out with Add microG support, whose account features need them.
name: Remove permissions

description: Removes Google's sign-in prompts: the first-launch "Make it your map" page, the search screen's "Tired of typing?" card and the account sheet's "Sign in" pill. Tapping "Your profile" (or the pill, where it still shows) answers with a "Can't sign in" toast instead of nothing. Left out with Add microG support, which signs in.
name: Remove sign-in prompts

description: Points the Firebase Installations and Play services compliance check-ins at an unresolvable host, stops every ad impression and click ping from being sent, and deregisters Google's logging, performance-monitoring, survey and Location History libraries and the on-device federated-learning services. With Add microG support, Firebase Installations and Location History are left alone, so Timeline, account sync and push messages keep working.
name: Remove telemetry

description: Turns on Waze's own switch for correcting the speed limit from the speedometer, the old mods' "Report speed limit". Waze's server keeps it off; what it shows is not verified here.
name: Report speed limit

description: Hands the alerts Waze is tracking -- police, crashes, hazards, traffic jams, closures and speed cameras -- to Ungoogled Maps on the same phone, where Waze alerts in Waze Features puts them on the map. Nothing leaves the phone. Waze has to be signed in and open; in the background is enough.
name: Share alerts with Maps

description: Plays the speed camera sound for every camera, not only when you are over the speed limit.
name: Speed camera sound at any speed

description: Chimes and shows a note when a speed or red light camera is coming up ahead, and puts the cameras on the map, from OpenStreetMap. Off until turned on in Waze Features, a row on the account sheet, because it downloads the cameras near you from an OpenStreetMap server.
name: Speed cameras

description: Turns speed camera and police alerts back on in the countries where Waze's server switches them off. Warning of speed cameras is against the law in some of those countries.
name: Speed cameras everywhere

description: The style of the speed limit sign beside the speedometer, whatever the country.
name: Speed limit sign

options.description: Waze picks one by country.
options.title: Sign style

description: Plays a chime when your speed passes the speed limit during navigation, as Waze does. Maps itself only turns its speedometer red. When it chimes is chosen in Waze Features, a row on the account sheet.
name: Speeding chime

description: Lets Waze keep running in the background without a route for the chosen time -- Waze's server allows 10 minutes -- so that its alerts keep reaching Maps while you navigate there. Costs battery; Waze still closes itself when you close it.
name: Stay awake in the background

options.description: How long Waze may run in the background without a route. Waze: 10.
options.title: Minutes in the background

description: Adds a Theme choice to the Experimental screen: Follow phone, Light, Dark or AMOLED black (dark with pure black backgrounds). AllTrails itself only follows the phone.
name: Theme

description: Removes Your Timeline, Location sharing, Your data in Maps and Help & feedback from the account sheet. Left out with Add microG support, whose account features need them.
name: Trim account menu

description: Shows the alerts a Waze on the same phone is tracking -- police to begin with, and any of crashes, hazards, traffic jams, closures and speed cameras -- as pins on the map, with a chime and a note as one comes up ahead. Off until turned on in Waze Features. Waze has to be patched with Share alerts with Maps, signed in and open; in the background is enough.
name: Waze alerts

description: Adds +, − and reset tiles during turn-by-turn that change the navigation zoom while the camera keeps following the car.
name: Zoom controls in navigation

description: Unlock Reclub Supporter via backend entitlements API and RevenueCat bridge.
name: Unlock premium

description: Adds Sort (off / most rated / top rated), 4★+, Hide ads and a 'Ranked' list to Amazon search pages. The ranked list covers every page loaded and can fetch more pages.

description: Adds Sort (off / most rated / top rated), 4★+, Hide ads and a 'Ranked' list to Flipkart listings. The ranked list orders every page the app has loaded.
name: Sort by number of ratings

description: Adds Sort (off / most rated / top rated), 4★+, Hide ads and a 'Ranked' list to Meesho catalog, search and collection feeds. The ranked list orders every page the app has loaded.
name: Sort by number of ratings

description: Adds Sort (off / most rated / top rated), 4★+, Hide ads and a 'Ranked' list to Myntra search and listing pages. The ranked list orders every page the app has loaded.
name: Sort by number of ratings

description: Unlock Reclub Supporter via backend entitlements API and RevenueCat bridge.
name: Unlock premium

name: 5.1-channel audio bridge (4XVR)

description: Rewrites native Oculus face/eye permission checks to the Android XR names, on exact 2.0.20/5001712, 2.0.20/5001812, 2.0.21/5001968 and 2.0.22/5002244 builds.

description: Legacy overlay fallback for older builds: adds SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW and the compositor signal window.
name: Appear on top (legacy)

description: Installs the bundled 5.1-channel AAudio bridge native for exact 4XVR 2.0.22 build 20022.
name: Audio bridge payload (4XVR)

description: Adds static blue noise after video colour processing and fade, on the background/base layer only; 8-bit or 10-bit input, always 8-bit sRGB output. Selectable per layer, but turn OLED's VD-like fovea options off when combining. Unknown host shaders pass through unchanged.
name: Background blue-noise dithering (experimental)

options.description: Both choices apply the same final 8-bit output quantizer. This describes your stream; it does not change host negotiation or decoder precision. When combining with OLED calibration, leave both of its existing VD-like fovea toggles off.
options.title: Declared input depth

description: Renames the package and Steam Link's internal VR-launch component, so the patched app can be installed next to the original.
name: Change package name

options.description: Accepts either a full Java package name (for example, com.valvesoftware.steamlinkvr.galaxyxr) or a display suffix (for example, Galaxy XR). Suffix input appends to app name and generates a package suffix automatically.
options.title: Package name

description: Adapts already corrected OpenXR angular velocity to Steam Link 2.0.23's local controller axes. Requires the active Galaxy XR OpenXR Velocity Frame runtime module; do not use with stock runtime velocities or old HAL/velocity/extrapolation APK layers. Changes angular velocity only, not poses, linear velocity or prediction. Exact 2.0.23/5002363 only; headset A/B validation pending.
name: Controller angular world to local, 2.0.23 (experimental)

description: Routes controller vibration to the grip vibrator instead of the trigger, which Galaxy XR uses for every OpenXR vibration. The grip one needs shell rights, so this needs Shizuku running with its permission granted to Steam Link; without it vibration is stock.
name: Controller grip haptics through Shizuku (experimental)

description: Makes the Galaxy XR runtime extrapolate controller poses to the time VRLink asks, instead of repeating one sample per display frame, and filters jitter out of the streamed pose. Adds an OpenXR API layer; no Steam Link code changes.
name: Controller pose extrapolation (experimental)

description: Takes controller poses straight from the Galaxy XR controller HAL instead of the OpenXR runtime, removing the runtime's ~35 ms sample lag, and filters jitter out of pose and velocity. The HAL needs shell rights, so this needs Shizuku running with its permission granted to Steam Link; without Shizuku tracking stays as it is. Steam Link 2.0.23: angular velocity is reported local to the grip pose.
name: Controller tracking from the controller HAL through Shizuku (experimental)

description: Takes controller poses straight from the Galaxy XR controller HAL instead of the OpenXR runtime, removing the runtime's ~35 ms sample lag, and filters jitter out of pose and velocity. The HAL needs shell rights, so this needs Shizuku running with its permission granted to Steam Link; without Shizuku tracking stays as it is. Steam Link 2.0.20 - 2.0.22: angular velocity is reported in the base space.
name: Controller tracking from the controller HAL through Shizuku, 2.0.20 - 2.0.22 (experimental)

description: Derives controller linear and angular velocity from grip/aim pose history, and can cut VRLink's 4 controller pose sends per display frame to 2 or 1.
name: Controller velocity fix

options.description: libgxr_controller_velocity.so config+32 (int64 ns = value×1e6). Falls back to runtime velocity when pose samples are farther apart. Allowed range: 5 to 100 ms.
options.title: Maximum sample gap (ms)

options.description: libvrlink_scene.so QSVLClient::OnTopOfFrame: selects four, two, or one evenly phased controller pose sends per display frame. Actual send Hz equals display Hz multiplied by 4, 2, or 1. Stock preserves Valve behavior.
options.title: Controller pose-send cadence

options.description: libgxr_controller_velocity.so config+48 (float32 EMA weight). 0 = no smoothing, minimum lag; higher values reduce jitter. Allowed range: 0.0 to 0.9.
options.title: Derived velocity smoothing

options.description: libgxr_controller_velocity.so config+40 (float32 m/s). Falls back to runtime velocity above this derived linear speed. Allowed range: 1 to 50 m/s.
options.title: Maximum linear speed (m/s)

options.description: libgxr_controller_velocity.so config+44 (float32 rad/s). Falls back to runtime velocity above this derived angular speed. Allowed range: 1 to 100 rad/s.
options.title: Maximum angular speed (rad/s)

description: Rotates the controller velocities the Galaxy XR runtime reports into the frames SteamVR reads, so thrown objects leave in the right direction. Stock, they arrive in a controller-attached frame. Adds an OpenXR API layer; no Steam Link code is changed. Steam Link 2.0.23: angular velocity is reported local to the streamed pose.
name: Controller velocity frame (experimental)

description: Rotates the controller velocities the Galaxy XR runtime reports into the frames SteamVR reads, so thrown objects leave in the right direction. Stock, they arrive in a controller-attached frame. Adds an OpenXR API layer; no Steam Link code is changed. Steam Link 2.0.20 - 2.0.22: angular velocity is reported in the base space.
name: Controller velocity frame, 2.0.20 - 2.0.22 (experimental)

description: Re-exposes the stock 4XVR launcher artwork under the canonical ic_launcher/ic_launcher_round names (adaptive icon plus density PNGs) and points the manifest at them, matching the Steam Link icon shape for exact 4XVR 2.0.22 build 20022.

dependencies: Startup splash and XR launch mode (before 5002322)

name: Galaxy XR legacy foundation (through 2.0.22/5002244)

dependencies: Startup splash and XR launch mode (before 5002322)

dependencies: Startup splash and XR launch mode (before 5002322)

dependencies: Startup splash and XR launch mode (before 5002322)

name: Galaxy XR recommended set (2.0.21/5001968)

name: Galaxy XR recommended set (2.0.23/5002363)

name: Galaxy XR set (4XVR 2.0.22/20022)

description: Installs libgxr_face_bridge.so, mapping XR_FB_face_tracking2 to XR_ANDROID_face_tracking, and adds FACE_TRACKING to the manifest on builds up to 5002318. Feeds the Galaxy XR VRCFT module.
name: GXR face bridge (version 5002318 and below)

name: GXR tongue bridge (version 5002322 and above)

name: libplacebo HDR pipeline (4XVR)

The reference Galaxy XR build requires the Meta platform channel to stay inert on a non-Meta runtime; launch-criticality is unproven and Meta-store VIP flows degrade. Default off; verify on device before enabling.
name: Meta platform decoupling (4XVR, experimental)

description: Selects Steam Link's AAudio microphone processing mode. On Galaxy XR, Voice Recognition was clearer and louder than stock Voice Communication.
name: Microphone input preset

options.description: Voice Recognition was the clearest usable-level mode in Galaxy XR recordings. Voice Performance and Unprocessed were substantially quieter; Voice Communication sounded more processed.
options.title: Microphone mode

description: Applies OLED gamma/saturation calibration with 8-bit sRGB output, plus optional VD-like SDR foveal processing and a separate foveal gamma. Exact builds 5001712, 5001812, 5001968, 5002244, 5002363; visible improvement needs headset verification.
name: OLED color calibration

options.description: Selects gamma and saturation for both layers when the VD options are off, or for the base layer when a VD foveal option is on.
options.title: Calibration profile

options.description: Used by Custom profile. Allowed range: 0.50 to 2.50.
options.title: Gamma

options.description: Used by Custom profile. Allowed range: 0.00 to 3.00.
options.title: Saturation

options.description: VD-informed SDR processing for declared 10-bit input: use highp sampling, retain Valve's decoder colour correction, bypass the calibration profile on the foveal layer, and add no shader noise. The separate foveal gamma adjustment still applies. Output is 8-bit sRGB. Does not negotiate host depth or reproduce VD's raw-YUV decoder import. Mutually exclusive with the 8-bit option and separate blue-noise patch.
options.title: Fovea VD-Like Input 10 bit

options.description: Uses the same VD-informed SDR foveal processing for declared 8-bit input, retaining Valve's decoder colour correction while bypassing the calibration profile and adding no shader noise. The separate foveal gamma adjustment still applies. Output is 8-bit sRGB. Cannot recover precision already lost in the source. Mutually exclusive with the 10-bit option and separate blue-noise patch; does not negotiate host depth.
options.title: Fovea VD-Like Input 8 bit

options.description: Additional gamma on the foveal layer only, after its colour processing. 1.00 leaves it unchanged; higher values darken shadows and midtones. Try 1.02 first for a lighter foveal region. Works with either VD option or both off, before fade and optional blue-noise dithering. Background calibration and edge blending stay unchanged; this is manual compensation, not a verified seam fix.
options.title: Foveal gamma adjustment

description: Installs the 4XVR render dispatch native (frame-synced scene queue and adaptive theater background updates) for exact 4XVR 2.0.22 build 20022.
name: Render dispatch payload (4XVR)

Leaves AWS Amplify, Firebase core/RemoteConfig/FCM and Google Ads init untouched so app data, push and the remote ad-config the ads patch relies on keep working.

Leaves Firebase core (FCM push, RemoteConfig) and the Facebook ContentProvider intact. Separate from the bytecode Block trackers patch so you can pick either or both.
name: Block trackers (manifest flags)

description: Bypasses foodpanda's DeliveryHero MAS integrity block — forces the master security gate (`w9u.a`) to report the device/app as trusted, so re-signed / sideloaded builds no longer hit the "This device or application is not supported" BlockedActivity.
name: Bypass anti-tamper (foodpanda)

description: Neutralizes the client-side device-validation gate (anti-root / anti-emulator / anti-Frida / anti-Xposed / anti-tamper battery) that shows a "Device validation failed" toast and kills the app via finishAffinity() on a rooted, emulated or re-signed build. Redirects the single failure callback to the success path so all ~16 checks report as passed and the app keeps running pre- and post-login.
name: Bypass device validation

description: Bypasses Google Play's PairIP license check so a re-signed Safar build runs instead of being blocked by the "Get this app from Play" paywall or a "Something went wrong" dialog.
name: Bypass license verification

description: Disables Google PairIP's license/installer check (com.pairip.licensecheck) so a re-signed build runs on a real device instead of being redirected to the Play Store and killed. No-ops the LicenseContentProvider entry point and LicenseClient.initializeLicenseCheck().
name: Bypass PairIP license check

description: Disables Simosa's anti-tamper signature check so a re-signed APK launches normally instead of stalling on the splash / "version is not correct" dialog.
name: Bypass signature verification

description: Forces OLX into dark (night) mode regardless of the system theme, using the app's built-in -night resources via UiModeManager.setApplicationNightMode at startup.
name: Force dark mode

description: Removes foodpanda's order-tracking ads (DeliveryHero adtech) and the forced, repeatedly-reappearing PandaMart "CrossSell" promo popup on the order-tracking screen.
name: Remove ads

description: Removes every AdMob ad — the interstitial (rerouted to its onAdFailedToLoad branch so the proxy-apply action still runs, but no ad loads or shows) and the on-screen banner (load skipped). No feature is lost.
name: Remove ads
